title: FOMC holds rates steady, markets rise modestly
full_text:
NEW YORK, Oct 28 (Reuters) - The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, awaiting further data on the path of inflation, and said it would reduce its policy-meeting schedule starting next year.
In a 10-2 decision, the US central bank said it would maintain its benchmark interest rate within the current 3.75%-4% range while acknowledging that inflation "remains elevated," upgrading its assessment of the economy and hinting that further rate hikes may be coming depending on inflation.
"The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s 2% goal," the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee said in its latest policy statement. "The Committee will deliver price stability."
Fed Governor Lisa Cook, currently targeted by President Donald Trump for removal from the central bank, dissented in favor of a quarter-percentage-point rate hike, as did Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, a consistently hawkish voice who also dissented in July for the same reason.
The Fed’s latest policy statement is a notable change from the September 15-16 meeting, with a hint of the sort of forward guidance Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has said he wants to avoid.
The Fed’s assessment of the economy was upgraded to "strong" from the "solid" expansion seen as of the September meeting, while investment was still viewed as robust and job gains were keeping pace with the workforce.
REACTION:
STOCKS: US stock indexes rose after Warsh began speaking, with the Nasdaq composite and the S&P 500 up 0.2%.
BONDS: Treasury yields pulled back then steepened after Warsh started his press conference, with the 2-year yield that’s most sensitive to Fed policy down 3.8 basis points to 4.7%, the 10-year yield up 5 basis points to 5.042% and the 30-year yield up 6 basis points at 5.367%.
FOREX: The US dollar index was off 0.2%.
COMMENTS:
TOM GRAFF, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, FACET, PHOENIX, MARYLAND:
“As expected, the Fed held rates at this meeting, setting up what is likely to be a hike in December. I believe this was a mistake: the Fed should have hiked today. Because Warsh decided to eschew forward guidance, his actions have to do all the talking. Another Fed Chair could have passed on a hike this meeting and still shown resolve to fight inflation by promising hikes down the road. Warsh has ceded that option.
"That means he needs to act sooner rather than later. Inflation remains high, without any obvious sign it’s subsiding, and I don’t think the recent spike in diesel prices has fully flowed into consumer inflation yet. If inflation is too high, what is the benefit of waiting? There isn’t any material difference between hiking now and hiking in December, especially since a December hike is fully priced in. Hiking today would have bolstered Warsh’s credibility as an inflation fighter. By waiting, he risks coming off as hesitant, or worse, complacent.”
RONALD GESTIEHR, DIRECTOR OF WEALTH MANAGEMENT, LUTTNER FINANCIAL, PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA:
"I believe they made the the right decision today. The economy remains resilient, inflation is a large concern, especially with everything going on with energy prices and the Middle East. They are walking a fine line on continuing to raise rates, they don’t want to go too far, too fast, and then cause us to slip into a recession.
"Raising rates does add pressure on individual consumers already hurt by inflation, especially considering lending rates."
KAREN MANNA, FIXED INCOME INVESTMENT STRATEGIST, FEDERATED HERMES, PITTSBURGH:
“By holding rates steady, the Fed has effectively deferred the debate rather than settled it. The market’s attention now shifts to December, incoming economic data, and any signals that clarify the Fed’s reaction function. Beyond the near-term outlook, investors will increasingly focus on the work of the Task Forces and the composition of the 2027 FOMC, both of which could shape the trajectory of policy over the coming years.”
CHRIS ZACCARELLI, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, NORTHLIGHT ASSET MANAGEMENT, CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA:
“Although the Fed held off on raising rates today, as we expected, they left plenty of clues that they were planning to raise rates in December. As always, a lot can change in the data between now and then, but if it weren’t so close to the midterm elections, they probably would have raised rates today, and now it’s unlikely that anything will stop them from raising rates at the next meeting.
"Next year, the picture is less clear. The futures are predicting two more rate hikes, and that makes sense if everything stays the same, but as we have learned over the past couple of years, things rarely do (e.g. tariffs, Iran war, etc). It’s our expectation that the economy will eventually run into some issues as rates move higher and the AI buildout is impacted.
"If we have a growth slowdown or recession in the next 12 months, then of course the Fed will react and we will see lower interest rates by the end of next year, but if the economy continues to be resilient despite all of the macroeconomic headwinds, then the Fed may end up raising even more than the 2 times that are currently priced in.”
SHAWN SNYDER, ECONOMIC STRATEGIST, POTOMAC FUND MANAGEMENT, BETHESDA, MARYLAND:
“The Fed appeared to upgrade its assessment of the economic outlook, describing economic activity as expanding at a "strong" rather than a "solid" pace. Of course, that raises the obvious question: If the economy is so strong and inflation remains stubborn, why not hike now?
"It seems highly unlikely that the inflation outlook will improve materially between now and December. Perhaps the Chair simply wants to give the task forces more time to reach their conclusions before taking the next step.
“For investors concerned about financing pressures in AI infrastructure, today’s decision to hold rates is unlikely to provide much relief. Thus far, credit-market distress has been concentrated among the weakest borrowers, but the enormous capital requirements of the AI buildout increasingly appear headed for a collision with elevated borrowing costs. That could leave some of the smaller fish in the AI pond going belly-up, while the bigger, better-capitalized fish keep swimming along just fine.
“We continue to believe hard assets are attractive in the current environment. When elevated inflation causes stocks and bonds to become more correlated, hard assets can provide an important source of portfolio diversification."
DAVID KRAKAUER, VICE PRESIDENT OF PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT, MERCER ADVISORS, SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA:
“A hold on rates, but not a dovish one. The vote was 10-2, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Cook’s dissent is the surprise, since many expected Hammack and Logan to be the hawks. The wording was also constructive on the economy. The statement described activity as expanding at a strong pace and spending as resilient, and it called productivity growth strong and capital investment robust. That doesn’t sound like a Fed worried about growth. It sounds like a Fed that believes the economy can handle tighter policy, which is why the debate is about when to hike, not whether.
“Stay in your seat. The hold doesn’t change the fundamentals: earnings growth for equities still looks attractive, and fixed income portfolios are now paying material real yields. Both point toward staying invested. With less forward guidance from Warsh, the path may be bumpy, but investors are being paid to be patient."
BILL MANN, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST, MOTLEY FOOL ASSET MANAGEMENT, VIENNA, VIRGINIA:
“We were pretty sure we were going to see a fight inside the house. The really interesting part was that they felt like they needed ’more information,’ which suggests to me that there is wild disagreement over how much petroleum prices are impacting inflation. You can’t fix a geopolitical imbalance with a monetary action.
“The 2% inflation goal seems a little performative. I don’t think that goal is what is most important for the Fed right now.”
BRIAN JACOBSEN, CHIEF ECONOMIC STRATEGIST, ANNEX WEALTH MANAGEMENT, MENOMONEE FALLS, WISCONSIN:
"It was a little surprising to see a governor dissent, but it was more surprising to see the statement upgrade the economic growth description from ’solid’ to ’strong.’
"In the Fed’s hierarchy, from weakest to strongest, it goes contraction to modest to moderate to solid to strong.
"What are they looking at to give the economy an upgrade? The moving average of weekly payroll gains from ADP was trending up between the July and September meeting, but it has been trending down since. The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow forecast has gone from white hot to merely smoldering.
"Maybe that’s why what could have been construed as forward guidance in the statement is now decidedly vague. More information will help them determine the policy stance, but last time, by saying the Fed ’removed a dose of accommodation’ implied that the Fed funds rate was still too low. Now it’s up in the air."
JAMIE COX, MANAGING PARTNER, HARRIS FINANCIAL GROUP, RICHMOND, VIRGINIA:
"The Federal Reserve just told markets that its rate hike expectations might be overzealous for what it’s likely to deliver. Data dependency is Fedspeak for "we don’t want to do anything unless we are forced to."
KARL SCHAMOTTA, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, CORPAY, TORONTO:
“Two dissents rather than the three or four many had expected is a dovish surprise at the margin, but an apparent upgrade in the Fed’s assessment of the economy itself should leave markets in no doubt that more tightening is coming.”
KAY HAIGH, GLOBAL HEAD, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF FIXED INCOME AND LIQUIDITY SOLUTIONS, GOLDMAN SACHS ASSET MANAGEMENT, NEW YORK:
“We expect the Fed to resume rate hikes in December. September’s strong CPI print is a reminder that upside inflation risks remain, and the Fed is likely to look to take out further insurance. While the September dot-plot suggests just one more hike, another increase in energy prices or further strong data prints could bring additional tightening into play next year.”
CHARLIE WISE, HEAD OF GLOBAL RESEARCH AND CONSULTING, TRANSUNION, CHICAGO:
“Today’s Federal Reserve decision to leave interest rates unchanged reflects the continued balancing act between inflation concerns and an economy and employment situation that have remained relatively resilient. Despite recent inflation readings coming in higher than expected, and well above the Fed’s target levels, policymakers opted to hold rates steady as they assess the impact of the September rate increase and monitor stable labor market conditions.
"For consumers, a pause in rate hikes means credit card borrowing costs are not increasing for now, but interest rate risk has not disappeared. title: Fed’s Warsh says US economy not running too hot

title: Microsoft stock up over 2% after hours as Azure strength drives FQ1 results beat
full_text:
Investing.com -- Microsoft on Wednesday delivered a quarterly top- and bottom-line beat, as continued strength in its Azure cloud unit helped keep concerns over artificial intelligence spending at bay.
Shares of the company climbed nearly 2.5% after hours.
"The all-important Azure growth rate beat expectations, signifying MSFT’s AI monetization efforts have progressed well. This could potentially fuel other areas of the AI trade but certainly is the large driver of the positive post market move we are seeing," Ryan Lee, senior vice president of product and strategy at Direxion, said.
The software giant’s results come at a time when spending on artificial intelligence has been under intense scrutiny. Concerns have soared over the billions of dollars being poured into AI infrastructure, or the combined hardware and software stack needed to handle massive data and computing power used to build and train AI processes.
Worries have also increased about the huge amounts of debt being issued by companies to fund these AI infrastructure buildouts, which in turn has contributed to a sell-off in government debt in the U.S. and across the world.
MSFT gained an early foothold in the AI industry boom after investing in ChatGPT developer OpenAI. It has since expanded its own AI product portfolio by developing its own models, diversifying its cloud infrastructure, launching AI agents, and integrating AI into its core products.
The world’s third-largest company has also in the process become a so-called AI hyperscaler, investing heavily in building and operating large-scale data centers. Other AI hyperscalers include Meta Platforms, Alphabet, Amazon, and Oracle. Last quarter, Microsoft was the only one to not raise capital expenditure forecasts.
MSFT earned $4.89 per share on revenue of $92.28 billion for its FQ1 2027. Analysts had expected a profit of $4.72 per share on revenue of $90.61 billion.
Even as AI takes over the spotlight, the growth engine for Microsoft remains its Azure cloud computing services business. Azure surpassed $100 billion in revenue in MSFT’s fiscal year 2026.
In FQ1 2027, Azure revenue jumped 48% Y/Y, helping overall Microsoft Cloud revenue improve 31% Y/Y in constant currency to $63.9 billion.
“We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack. By helping organizations build and own their own intelligence, and earning trust through agent safety and security, we are translating our innovation into growing adoption and real-world impact across every industry,” MSFT top boss Satya Nadella said in a statement.

title: Alphabet shares tumble 8.5% as earnings miss overshadows cloud boom
full_text:
Investing.com -- Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) shares fell 8.5% Wednesday after the Google parent reported third-quarter earnings well below Wall Street expectations, as investment losses and rising costs weighed on profitability despite strong revenue growth and accelerating demand for AI services.
Alphabet reported earnings per share of $2.12, missing the analyst consensus of $3.02 by $0.90. Revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, narrowly beating estimates of $127.22 billion.
The earnings shortfall reflected a sharp deterioration in non-operating income, alongside higher expenses. Alphabet swung to an $8.2 billion net expense from $12.8 billion in net other income a year earlier. The company recorded an $8.7 billion loss on equity securities, reducing net income by $6.7 billion, or $0.55 per diluted share, after tax.
Operating performance was stronger, with operating income rising 30% to $40.6 billion. However, research and development expenses climbed to $20.6 billion from $15.2 billion a year earlier. The earnings release does not provide a reconciliation showing how much each factor contributed to the $0.90 consensus EPS miss.
CEO Sundar Pichai said Alphabet was now at a half-trillion-dollar annual revenue run rate, as AI adoption gains momentum across its businesses. Customers of Gemini Enterprise more than quadrupled their spending year over year, while more than 90% of Fortune 100 companies use the platform, Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said on the earnings call.
Google Cloud revenue surged 103% to $30.7 billion, while operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion. The division now has 18 product lines generating more than $1 billion in annual sales, Kurian said.
Pichai also highlighted progress in Google’s AI models. The company’s new Carbon model outperforms Gemini 4 Argon and is being tested with the U.S. government, with an initial rollout planned for cybersecurity partners. Meanwhile, search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, he said.
Yet Alphabet’s AI expansion is putting increasing pressure on cash generation. Capital expenditures reached $51.4 billion in the quarter, up from $24 billion a year earlier, bringing year-to-date spending to $132 billion. The company maintained its full-year capital expenditure forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion, broadly in line with the $202.21 billion analyst consensus.
Free cash flow turned negative at $9.1 billion, with spending on infrastructure, TPU inventory and an EU fine contributing to the cash outflow. Alphabet also disclosed $924 billion in future purchase commitments, highlighting the scale of its obligations as it expands infrastructure to meet AI demand.
The results leave investors balancing accelerating cloud growth and expanding AI adoption against rising infrastructure costs, substantial future commitments and volatile investment returns. The sharp share-price decline suggests that strong demand alone is not enough: investors also want evidence that Alphabet’s AI investments can translate into sustained earnings and cash flow.

title: Cyberattack concealed political spending by big donors before US midterm elections
full_text:
By Dawn Kopecki
NEW YORK, Oct 28 (Reuters) - The Federal Election Commission restored its electronic filing system Wednesday night after taking it offline for nearly 41 hours to contain a cyberattack, which temporarily concealed spending from big donors as political donations ramp up in the final days of the midterms.
Campaign watchdogs sounded alarms as the outage dragged into its third evening. Super PACs and other groups could not file mandatory 24- and 48-hour reports that show how much money they are spending to help or hurt candidates at the polls, shrouding the most recent political spending from public view.
"We didn’t have access to the last-minute spending, which is really ramped up as the election draws nearer," said campaign finance watchdog Molly White, who tracks crypto and Big Tech political spending. "We have no visibility into that when the filing systems are down."
"It’s pretty devastating this close to the election," she added.
The outage came at a critical time as daily spending accelerates to its fastest pace in the two-year election cycle, campaign finance experts said. Super PACs, which can accept and give unlimited amounts of money, and dark money groups spent an average of over $50 million per day the week before the outage, OpenSecrets research director Brendan Glavin said. More than $250 million in spending was reported on October 20 alone, he added.
The FEC told users that most of the services affected by the outage have been restored. It posted a notice just after 10 p.m. ET on Monday saying it was investigating a problem that caused "major" outages across its systems that process electronic campaign filings.
Reuters could not establish the motive for the hacking effort. Hackers of all stripes regularly target government networks for espionage, financial gain or political motives.
The FEC does not play a role in administering US elections and the outage should have no effect on voters’ ability to cast ballots.
“Disclosure delayed is disclosure denied,” Hilary Braseth, executive director of nonpartisan campaign finance watchdog OpenSecrets, said in a statement released before the system was restored. “When hundreds of millions of dollars in outside money flood political airwaves in the final days before an election, transparency is not an optional luxury, it is a fundamental public safeguard.”
The FEC did not return requests for comment Wednesday and did not announce any details on the cause of the outage. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the FBI both referred questions to the FEC.
An FEC officer told campaign compliance firms late Monday that it took those services offline after a "bad actor" tried to breach the agency’s systems, according to an email reviewed by Reuters.
Campaign finance managers had to reset their passwords before logging in to the system, according to an email reviewed by Reuters.
The timing of the hacking attempt this close to the November 3 elections, and lack of information from the FEC, stirred up conspiracy theories throughout the industry, several people said. White noted that it would be a good way for unscrupulous actors to hide unpopular last-minute spending.
"It’s hard to say with any real information that that’s what happened, but it’s certainly I think where people’s minds go very quickly," she said.
Kyle Sandy, the cybersecurity director at IT security firm Logically, said taking the system offline is the right call when dealing with an attack.
"It tells me the FEC detected something they couldn’t immediately scope and chose a known outage over an unknown risk," Sandy said, giving the agency time to ensure none of its data was altered by the hackers before bringing it back online.

title: Utah criminally charges Kalshi with promoting illegal gambling
full_text:
By Nate Raymond
Oct 28 (Reuters) - Utah’s attorney general brought criminal charges against Kalshi and two of its top executives, accusing the prediction market platform of illegally promoting online gambling and allowing an undercover agent to place wagers on sports events.
Utah Attorney General Derek Brown, a Republican, filed the charges against Kalshi and its two co-founders, Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara, a day after the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued to block the state from enforcing its anti-gambling laws against the company.
"Gambling is illegal in Utah, whether you place the bet, run the game, or promote it," Brown said in a statement. "Calling it a ’prediction market’ doesn’t change what it is, and being federally registered doesn’t put a company above the law."
The charges, which were filed in a state court in Salt Lake County, mark an escalation for the state’s enforcement efforts, after Brown last week filed a lawsuit alleging Kalshi was allowing residents to illegally place bets on sports, elections and politics.
Kalshi has been at the center of an escalating legal battle over the ability of state gaming regulators to police companies in the fast-growing prediction markets industry.
While several states have engaged in litigation with Kalshi, only Arizona has previously pursued a criminal case, which was later blocked by a federal judge.
"This is a crazy overreach; Utah is clearly playing politics," a Kalshi spokesperson said. "We look forward to putting a stop to this in court, just like we did in Arizona."
The charges include one count of pattern of unlawful activity, a second-degree felony; 12 counts of online gambling promotion, a third-degree felony; and one count of general gambling promotion, a misdemeanor.
Charging documents cite 12 different instances in which an agent was allowed to place bets on football, baseball and other sports matches in September.
According to the charging papers, Kalshi has allowed Utah residents to place bets using its platform even after a federal judge in August ruled that federal law did not prevent Utah from enforcing its state gaming laws against the company.
Under Republican President Donald Trump’s administration, the CFTC has shared Kalshi’s position that trading on prediction markets falls exclusively under the agency’s jurisdiction.
That question has divided appeals courts and is likely to ultimately be decided by the US Supreme Court, which has been asked to resolve the issue.
